title: Turn a long parcel in place between two neighbours, then push it lengthwise into a taped bay
instruction: Get the long brown parcel into the red-taped bay, lying lengthwise with its long sides running front to back and its front end against the stop bar, and leave it there, without bumping the white boxes on either side of it.
context: Hand freight and stock movers (O*NET 53-7062.00, Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand) and parcel handlers on induction belts and packing benches often have to turn a long carton to fit a chute, scanner or lane while other parcels sit close beside it. Pushed at one end, a long box swings about a point near its other end and slides into its neighbours; turning it in place takes both hands pushing its two ends in opposite directions at once, and only then does it fit through the lane's entrance. Here the lane is a bay taped out on the table: its mouth, between two bollards, is narrower than the parcel is long, and it ends at a stop bar. The instruction only says where the parcel has to end up.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) The long parcel: a closed brown corrugated cardboard box, 42 cm long x 14 cm deep x 10 cm tall, 800 g, lying flat with its centre 30 cm forward on the centre line and its long sides parallel to the line between the bases. Turned about its centre, its corners sweep a circle 22.1 cm in radius. (2) Two white cardboard boxes, 20 cm wide x 14 cm deep x 10 cm tall, 1.2 kg each, centred 30 cm forward and 33.3 cm left and right of the centre line: their inner faces are 2.3 cm beyond the long parcel's ends. (3) Two yellow bollards (fixed posts 3 x 3 cm, 8 cm tall) centred 48 cm forward, 20 cm left and right: 37 cm apart inside, less than the parcel's length, and 2.7 cm clear of the circle its corners sweep. (4) The bay: red tape (1.5 cm wide, 0.5 mm thick) on the table outlining a rectangle 20 cm wide (inside the tape, centred on the centre line) from 20 to 66 cm forward; it runs under the parcel's start position. (5) A dark grey stop bar (fixed, 22 cm wide x 2 cm deep x 4 cm tall) across the bay's far end, its near face (toward the arms) 66 cm forward. The long parcel and the two white boxes are loose; the bollards, the stop bar and the tape are fixed. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead video and with a tape measure and a protractor; in the simulator the boxes' poses are read from the simulation, and the arms' collision shapes are placed from their measured joint positions. Two rules hold for the whole trial: if at any moment the long parcel's centre is more than 4 cm to either side of the centre line, or either white box has moved more than 1 cm, the trial scores 0. 1.0: the long parcel is let go (no part of either arm within 1 cm of it), lies flat on the table (each of the four corners of its underside within 3 mm of the table top), lies inside the bay (those four corners inside the red tape's inner edges, or at most 5 mm onto the tape), its long sides within 5 degrees of front to back, both corners of its front end within 1 cm of the stop bar, and it and both white boxes are at rest (moving slower than 1 cm/s and turning slower than 0.1 rad/s), all of this without a break for 2 s. 0.5: at the end of the trial the parcel is let go, lies flat on the table (as for 1.0) and is at rest, turned to within 10 degrees of front to back, but is not placed as for 1.0 (for instance it stopped more than 1 cm short of the stop bar). 0.0: anything else, including a parcel held or propped above the table, and any trial in which one of the two rules was broken.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: put the three cartons back on their start positions (tape marks on the table make this quick).
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the cartons are rigid, uniformly dense blocks (no flex or shifting contents), and the tape is a 0.5 mm raised strip. Loose objects get rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic); cardboard on a real table is nearer 0.4-0.5, so the pushes need less force. Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers went down at the parcel's two ends, next to the white boxes, and stayed over them for the rest of the trial; the parcel was never turned); demo: 1.0
